### Reader question

How should an engineer build and interpret an Agent Flamegraph so that its widths, semantic categories, input sessions, and privacy boundary are reproducible rather than merely visually plausible?

### Durable information gain

The refresh is pinned to AgentSight v1.0.25 and adds current first-party implementation details that are not present in the existing guide:

- `agentpprof` is an offline/rootless profiler of local Codex and Claude Code history through `agent-session`; it is not a live eBPF or CPU profiler;
- explicit `--session-file` inputs are preferred over a drifting project-history scan for repeatable publication;
- operations, tokens, time, files, and network views have different width units and different failure modes;
- the default stack is the operation-field projection `task,skill,phase,action,object,repeat,result,outcome`, with `project`, `agent`, and `session` retained as pprof labels;
- `--op-map`, `--where`, `--stack`, and related controls are part of the reproducible method because they change how samples merge;
- token width prefers source-reported counts and bounds unsafe text estimates rather than allowing an implausible estimate to dominate the chart;
- JSON previews are opt-in and privacy-sensitive, while out-of-project paths are grouped into stable `external/*` buckets;
- the shipped iterative-tagging skill supplies concrete diagnostics for unmatched coverage and category distribution, which are workflow heuristics rather than statistical guarantees;
- the first-party v1.0.25 token SVG is embedded as a format example and explicitly not presented as a benchmark for another workload.

Primary sources are the exact v1.0.25 `ext/pprof/README.md`, `docs/agentpprof.md`, `skills/agentpprof-flamegraph/SKILL.md`, and the pinned first-party flamegraph gallery at product commit `0080545f7c6b110ec2d4a4af5100b58f514c84d5`.
